news.title_original: A New Report From The Independent Panel - Hiding In Plain Sight: Mpox And The Cost Of Neglecting Known Threats

analysis.time: The report was published on Saturday, 31 October 2026, and discusses mpox outbreaks in 2026, with specific mention of Madagascar's outbreak as of mid-August 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The report covers mpox outbreaks in multiple countries, including the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Madagascar, with a global spread affecting 82 countries by 2026.
analysis.event: The Independent Panel's report highlights the global spread of mpox, the emergence of new variants, and the failure to prioritize control measures in endemic regions, leading to preventable health emergencies.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: As of mid-August 2026, Madagascar reported over 3,400 cases and 22 deaths. In the EU/EEA, nearly 3,800 confirmed mpox cases were reported in the last 12 months, with local transmission indicated. The report emphasizes the burden on health systems and the risks posed by mpox to vulnerable populations.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The report notes that vaccines were deployed in some countries during the 2024–2025 outbreaks but states it is unclear how much impact they had. A vaccine stockpile was announced in August 2026, and rapid diagnostic tests and therapies were not available where most needed.

analysis.brief_en: The Independent Panel's report, 'Hiding in Plain Sight: Mpox and the Cost of Neglecting Known Threats,' published on 31 October 2026, highlights the global spread of mpox, which has now become a widespread public health risk. The report states that mpox, once a sporadic disease in West and Central Africa, has caused outbreaks in 82 countries by 2026, with Madagascar facing the largest outbreak of 2026, reporting over 3,400 cases and 22 deaths as of mid-August. The report also notes that new variants of the monkeypox virus have emerged, increasing risks for people and straining health systems. It criticizes the failure to prioritize mpox control in endemic regions, particularly the Democratic Republic of the Congo, where health workers manage multiple challenges, including Ebola. The report emphasizes that vaccines were deployed in some countries during the 2024–2025 outbreaks but remains uncertain about their impact. A vaccine stockpile was announced in August 2026, but rapid diagnostic tests and therapies were not available where they were most needed. The report calls for sustained investment in community systems to prevent future health emergencies and better prepare for the next pandemic threat.

A vaccine stockpile was announced in August 2026, but rapid diagnostic tests and therapies were not available where they were most needed. The report calls for sustained investment in community systems to prevent future health emergencies and better prepare for the next pandemic threat.
news.content_zh: 独立小组发布的报告《显而易见的隐患:猴痘 与忽视已知威胁的成本》于 2026 年 10 月 31 日发表,强调了 猴痘 的全球传播,该病毒现已成为全球公共卫生风险。报告指出,猴痘 曾一度是西非和中非地区的偶发性疾病,但到 2026 年已导致 82 个国家出现 暴发,其中马达加斯加面临 2026 年最大的 暴发,截至 2026 年 8 月中旬,已报告超过 3,400 例病例和 22 例死亡。报告还指出,猴痘病毒的新变种已出现,增加了对人群的风险并给卫生系统带来压力。它批评了在疫区未能优先控制 猴痘 的情况,特别是在刚果民主共和国,卫生工作者需应对包括埃博拉在内的多种挑战。报告强调,某些国家在 2024–2025 年的 暴发 中部署了 疫苗,但对其影响仍存在不确定性。2026 年 8 月宣布了 疫苗 的储备,但快速诊断测试和治疗手段并未在最需要的地方提供。报告呼吁持续投资社区系统,以预防未来的公共卫生紧急情况,并更好地应对下一次大流行威胁。

news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Monday, November 2, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Chickenpox Virus Dominated Rash Illnesses Mistaken for Mpox in Sierra Leone by October 29, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 4 mins read 0 Chickenpox Virus Dominated Rash Illnesses Mistaken for Mpox in Sierra Leone Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram During Sierra Leone’s 2025 mpox epidemic, more than half of the patients who met the clinical case definition for mpox but tested negative for the mpox virus were carrying other rash-causing pathogens, with varicella-zoster virus — the agent of chickenpox and shingles — accounting for the vast majority of those detections. That is the central finding of a retrospective laboratory-based surveillance study published in New Microbes and New Infections, which screened samples from MPXV-negative suspected mpox cases using two commercial multiplex PCR panels across eight health districts. The study was conducted between June 16 and August 27, 2025, as part of the national epidemic response. Two mobile laboratories, deployed at the regional hospital in Port Loko and at the Koinadugu District Government Hospital, processed clinical specimens — predominantly lesion swabs, along with a small number of vaginal swabs and crust samples — from patients meeting the World Health Organization mpox case definition. During active case searching, the definition was broadened to include anyone presenting with a severe rash, even if other criteria were not met. In total, 407 suspected mpox cases were sampled and tested for MPXV by quantitative PCR during the study window. Of these, 144 were positive, corresponding to a positivity rate of 35.7 percent, and were excluded from the differential analysis. The remaining 263 MPXV-negative samples — 252 lesion swabs, seven vaginal swabs, and four crust samples — all passed an endogenous control quality check and were retained for further testing. Discover more Study Biology Check Symptoms Read Med Journals Find Skin Care Buy Maps The researchers used the Allplex Meningitis-V1 Assay, previously validated on cutaneous samples with next-generation sequencing, to detect seven herpesviruses: herpes simplex virus types 1 and 2, varicella-zoster virus, Epstein-Barr virus, cytomegalovirus, and human herpesviruses 6 and 7. A second panel, the Allplex Genital Ulcer Assay, targeted the bacteria Haemophilus ducreyi, Treponema pallidum, and Chlamydia trachomatis, the causative agent of lymphogranuloma venereum, alongside overlapping viral targets. A sample was considered positive if a target was detected with a cycle threshold value below 35, and weak or late amplification signals were re-tested in duplicate. For the four targets covered by both panels, duplicate testing yielded 100 percent concordance. The results showed that at least one target was identified in 153 of the 263 samples, an overall detection rate of 58.2 percent. Varicella-zoster virus was by far the most frequently detected pathogen, found in 43.3 percent of patients (114 of 263; 95 percent confidence interval 37.3 to 49.6). Among the other herpesviruses, HSV-2 showed the highest detection frequency at 7.2 percent, followed by cytomegalovirus at 6.85 percent and Epstein-Barr virus at 6.1 percent. Lower rates were recorded for HHV-7 (4.6 percent), HSV-1 (1.9 percent), and HHV-6 (0.4 percent). Among bacterial targets, Haemophilus ducreyi was detected in 1.1 percent of cases, while every sample tested negative for Treponema pallidum and Chlamydia trachomatis. The study population was young: ages ranged from 1 to 80 years with a median of 18 years, and 44.5 percent of participants were aged 15 or younger. Gender information was available for 259 participants, of whom 58.7 percent were male. Statistically significant associations with age emerged for Epstein-Barr virus and HSV-2, both detected at higher proportions in older age groups, with detection rising progressively across the three age strata. Cytomegalovirus and Epstein-Barr virus were the only pathogens showing significant sex-based differences, both more frequent among females. Varicella-zoster virus showed no significant demographic associations, although nearly 48 percent of children aged 15 or younger tested positive compared with 39 percent of patients over 30, a difference that did not reach statistical significance. Co-detections were common and often complex. Combinations involving varicella-zoster virus were the most frequent, occurring in 19 samples, most often alongside HSV-2 and cytomegalovirus. One sample was positive for five herpesviruses simultaneously — varicella-zoster virus, cytomegalovirus, HSV-2, HHV-7, and Epstein-Barr virus — and two samples carried triple viral infections. Haemophilus ducreyi was exclusively co-detected with varicella-zoster virus, on two occasions, a molecular co-detection the authors describe as rarely reported. Among co-detections not involving varicella-zoster virus, nine of ten included Epstein-Barr virus. The authors caution that, given the small numbers, no inference about biological interaction between co-detected pathogens can be made. Discover more Shop African Art Explore History Track Outbreaks Uninterruptible power supplies Applied science journals Geographically, the highest sample numbers came from Port Loko and Tonkolili, and detections of at least one target exceeded undiagnosed cases in five of the eight surveyed districts. Varicella-zoster virus was the only pathogen identified in every district where positive cases were found, with the largest counts in Koinadugu, Falaba, and Port Loko. The distribution of other pathogens varied: HSV-2 and cytomegalovirus clustered in Port Loko and Tonkolili, Epstein-Barr virus in Kambia, and HHV-7 in Kambia and Bombali. One observation carries particular public health weight. The retrospective screening identified Haemophilus ducreyi in three samples collected months before an outbreak of Haemophilus ducreyi-associated skin ulceration was officially declared in Sierra Leone for the first time in December 2025, with the reported likely index case showing symptom onset on October 1, 2025. The authors stress that their findings do not establish an epidemiological link between these three patients and the subsequent outbreak, but they argue that real-time differential testing could potentially have provided an early warning signal prompting further investigation. The study has notable limitations. Samples and epidemiological data were originally collected for the mpox response, leaving critical clinical information — including symptoms, HIV status, and patient outcomes — incomplete, so the clinical impact of co-detections could not be assessed. MPXV-positive samples were not included in the differential testing, sequencing was not performed, and the study period covered neither the entire outbreak timeline nor every district in Sierra Leone. The authors also note that pathogen distributions can vary seasonally, meaning the findings represent a temporal snapshot rather than a complete annual profile, which may partly explain the absence of Chlamydia trachomatis and Treponema pallidum detections. Even so, the results demonstrate the feasibility of integrating multiplex molecular screening into outbreak response, particularly when combined with mobile laboratory deployment, to reduce diagnostic dead ends and uncover pathogens circulating beneath the epidemiological signal of a dominant outbreak agent. That is the central finding of a retrospective laboratory-based surveillance study published in New Microbes and New Infections, which screened samples from MPXV-negative suspected mpox cases using two commercial multiplex PCR panels across eight health districts. The study was conducted between June 16 and August 27, 2025, as part of the national epidemic response. Two mobile laboratories, deployed at the regional hospital in Port Loko and at the Koinadugu District Government Hospital, processed clinical specimens — predominantly lesion swabs, along with a small number of vaginal swabs and crust samples — from patients meeting the World Health Organization mpox case definition. During active case searching, the definition was broadened to include anyone presenting with a severe rash, even if other criteria were not met. In total, 407 suspected mpox cases were sampled and tested for MPXV by quantitative PCR during the study window. Of these, 144 were positive, corresponding to a positivity rate of 35.7 percent, and were excluded from the differential analysis. The remaining 263 MPXV-negative samples — 252 lesion swabs, seven vaginal swabs, and four crust samples — all passed an endogenous control quality check and were retained for further testing. Discover more Study Biology Check Symptoms Read Med Journals Find Skin Care Buy Maps The researchers used the Allplex Meningitis-V1 Assay, previously validated on cutaneous samples with next-generation sequencing, to detect seven herpesviruses: herpes simplex virus types 1 and 2, varicella-zoster virus, Epstein-Barr virus, cytomegalovirus, and human herpesviruses 6 and 7. A second panel, the Allplex Genital Ulcer Assay, targeted the bacteria Haemophilus ducreyi, Treponema pallidum, and Chlamydia trachomatis, the causative agent of lymphogranuloma venereum, alongside overlapping viral targets. A sample was considered positive if a target was detected with a cycle threshold value below 35, and weak or late amplification signals were re-tested in duplicate. For the four targets covered by both panels, duplicate testing yielded 100 percent concordance. The results showed that at least one target was identified in 153 of the 263 samples, an overall detection rate of 58.2 percent. Varicella-zoster virus was by far the most frequently detected pathogen, found in 43.3 percent of patients (114 of 263; 95 percent confidence interval 37.3 to 49.6). Among the other herpesviruses, HSV-2 showed the highest detection frequency at 7.2 percent, followed by cytomegalovirus at 6.85 percent and Epstein-Barr virus at 6.1 percent. Lower rates were recorded for HHV-7 (4.6 percent), HSV-1 (1.9 percent), and HHV-6 (0.4 percent). Among bacterial targets, Haemophilus ducreyi was detected in 1.1 percent of cases, while every sample tested negative for Treponema pallidum and Chlamydia trachomatis. The study population was young: ages ranged from 1 to 80 years with a median of 18 years, and 44.5 percent of participants were aged 15 or younger. Gender information was available for 259 participants, of whom 58.7 percent were male. Statistically significant associations with age emerged for Epstein-Barr virus and HSV-2, both detected at higher proportions in older age groups, with detection rising progressively across the three age strata. Cytomegalovirus and Epstein-Barr virus were the only pathogens showing significant sex-based differences, both more frequent among females. Varicella-zoster virus showed no significant demographic associations, although nearly 48 percent of children aged 15 or younger tested positive compared with 39 percent of patients over 30, a difference that did not reach statistical significance. Co-detections were common and often complex. Combinations involving varicella-zoster virus were the most frequent, occurring in 19 samples, most often alongside HSV-2 and cytomegalovirus. One sample was positive for five herpesviruses simultaneously — varicella-zoster virus, cytomegalovirus, HSV-2, HHV-7, and Epstein-Barr virus — and two samples carried triple viral infections. Haemophilus ducreyi was exclusively co-detected with varicella-zoster virus, on two occasions, a molecular co-detection the authors describe as rarely reported. Among co-detections not involving varicella-zoster virus, nine of ten included Epstein-Barr virus. The authors caution that, given the small numbers, no inference about biological interaction between co-detected pathogens can be made. Discover more Shop African Art Explore History Track Outbreaks Uninterruptible power supplies Applied science journals Geographically, the highest sample numbers came from Port Loko and Tonkolili, and detections of at least one target exceeded undiagnosed cases in five of the eight surveyed districts. Varicella-zoster virus was the only pathogen identified in every district where positive cases were found, with the largest counts in Koinadugu, Falaba, and Port Loko. The distribution of other pathogens varied: HSV-2 and cytomegalovirus clustered in Port Loko and Tonkolili, Epstein-Barr virus in Kambia, and HHV-7 in Kambia and Bombali. One observation carries particular public health weight. The retrospective screening identified Haemophilus ducreyi in three samples collected months before an outbreak of Haemophilus ducreyi-associated skin ulceration was officially declared in Sierra Leone for the first time in December 2025, with the reported likely index case showing symptom onset on October 1, 2025. The authors stress that their findings do not establish an epidemiological link between these three patients and the subsequent outbreak, but they argue that real-time differential testing could potentially have provided an early warning signal prompting further investigation. The study has notable limitations. Samples and epidemiological data were originally collected for the mpox response, leaving critical clinical information — including symptoms, HIV status, and patient outcomes — incomplete, so the clinical impact of co-detections could not be assessed. MPXV-positive samples were not included in the differential testing, sequencing was not performed, and the study period covered neither the entire outbreak timeline nor every district in Sierra Leone. The authors also note that pathogen distributions can vary seasonally, meaning the findings represent a temporal snapshot rather than a complete annual profile, which may partly explain the absence of Chlamydia trachomatis and Treponema pallidum detections. Even so, the results demonstrate the feasibility of integrating multiplex molecular screening into outbreak response, particularly when combined with mobile laboratory deployment, to reduce diagnostic dead ends and uncover pathogens circulating beneath the epidemiological signal of a dominant outbreak agent. news.excerpt: Patients with nonsexually acquired clade II mpox experience higher hospitalization rates and HIV prevalence than those with sexually acquired disease.

news.content: Menu SECTIONS News Features CME Conferences Clinical Tools Special Collections Multimedia Fact Sheets Diagnosis & Disease Info Topics Abdominal Infections Bone and Joint Infections Cardiovascular Infections Central Nervous System Infections Covid 19 News & Insights Eye Infections Gastrointestinal Infections General Infectious Disease General Medicine Hepatitis HIV/AIDS Infection Control and Prevention Nosocomial Infections Pleuropulmonary and Bronchial Infections Practice Management Reproductive Organ Infections and Sexually Transmitted Infections Sepsis Skin and Soft Tissue Infection Upper Respiratory Tract Infections Urinary Tract Infection Vector-Borne Illnesses Haymarket Medical Network Cancer Therapy Advisor Cardiology Advisor Clinical Advisor Clinical Pain Advisor Dermatology Advisor Endocrinology Advisor Gastroenterology Advisor Hematology Advisor Infectious Disease Advisor Medical Bag MPR Neurology Advisor Obesity Advisor Oncology Nurse Advisor Ophthalmology Advisor Optometry Advisor Psychiatry Advisor Pulmonology Advisor Rare Disease Advisor Renal and Urology News Rheumatology Advisor Sleep Wake Advisor Vaccine Advisor Search for: COVID-19 News CME Drugs Calculators Charts Resources Multimedia Meetings Part of the News and Features CME Conferences Clinical Tools Special Collections Multimedia Share this article Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Share on LinkedIn Share on Bluesky Share by Email Print IDWeek Nonsexually Acquired Mpox Associated With Higher Hospitalization Rates Hibah Khaja, PharmD | Publish Date October 27, 2026 Researchers evaluated demographic and clinical differences between patients with sexually and nonsexually acquired clade II mpox in California. Compared with sexual transmission, nonsexually acquired clade II mpox is associated with an increased risk for hospitalization, a higher prevalence of HIV, and lower vaccination rates. Patients with clade II mpox (previously monkeypox) resulting from nonsexual transmission are more frequently hospitalized and have a higher prevalence of HIV than those who report recent sexual contact, according to study results presented at IDWeek 2026, held from October 21 to 24, in Washington, DC. Researchers evaluated differences in demographic characteristics, clinical outcomes, and potential exposures among patients with sexually and nonsexually acquired mpox in California. The analysis included confirmed and probable clade II mpox cases reported to the California Department of Public Health between May 2022 and December 2024. Drawing on public health surveillance records, the researchers sorted cases into groups based on whether patients reported sexual activity in the 21 days before their symptoms began. Patients who denied sexual contact during this period were included in the nonsexual exposure group only if their initial lesions occurred outside the genital and perianal regions. Those reporting no sexual contact but presenting with lesions initially involving these areas were excluded from that group. More information is needed on the dynamics of which populations may be at risk for non-sexual mpox transmission for targeted messaging and strategies. Demographic and clinical characteristics were compared using proportions via the Wilson method. Statistical significance was assessed based on whether the CIs overlapped between groups. Of 6651 reported mpox cases, 5206 had sufficient information to determine sexual exposure classification. Among these patients, 561 (10.8%) were categorized as having nonsexually acquired mpox, while 4645 (89.2%) reported recent sexual contact. Hospitalization occurred in 12.5% of patients in the nonsexual exposure group compared with 4.7% in the sexual exposure group. The prevalence of HIV was also higher among patients classified as having nonsexually acquired mpox (53.3% vs 39.8%). The researchers reported differences in vaccination history and potential environmental exposure. Most patients in both groups were unvaccinated against mpox, although the proportion was higher among those in the nonsexual group (96.8% vs 87.9%). Receipt of 1 vaccine dose was reported in 2.3% vs 5.6% of patients, respectively, while 0.9% vs 6.5% had received 2 doses. Possible exposure through contaminated objects or surfaces was reported by 16.4% of patients in the nonsexual group compared with 10.0% of those in the sexual exposure group. Patients classified as having nonsexually acquired mpox also differed by age, sex at birth, and race and ethnicity. The proportion assigned female at birth was higher in the nonsexual group (4.6% vs 2.2%), as was the proportion younger than 18 years (2.3% vs 0.3%). Black patients accounted for 17.5% of nonsexual cases and 10.8% of sexual cases, while Hispanic or Latino patients represented 53.5% and 43.5%, respectively. White patients accounted for a smaller proportion of the nonsexual group than the sexual exposure group (18.5% vs 32.2%). Regarding sexual orientation, 20.0% of patients in the nonsexual group identified as heterosexual compared with 7.3% of those in the sexual exposure group. Conversely, 54.2% vs 73.7% identified as gay, lesbian, or same-gender loving. Patients declining to disclose their sexual orientation represented 5.9% and 5.4% of the respective groups. Geographic socioeconomic differences were identified using the Health Performance Index (HPI). Residence in an area within the lowest HPI quartile was more common among patients in the nonsexual group (38.5% vs 23.4%), whereas residence in the highest quartile was less common (14.5% vs 27.9%). All reported differences were considered statistically significant based on nonoverlapping 95% CIs. “More information is needed on the dynamics of which populations may be at risk for non-sexual mpox transmission for targeted messaging and strategies,” the researchers concluded. analysis.time: The study was conducted between May 2022 and December 2024, with the publication date on October 27, 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The study focused on mpox cases in California, comparing patients with nonsexually acquired mpox to those with sexually acquired mpox, including demographic and clinical characteristics.
analysis.event: Researchers evaluated demographic and clinical differences between patients with sexually and nonsexually acquired clade II mpox in California, finding that nonsexually acquired cases were associated with higher hospitalization rates, higher HIV prevalence, and lower vaccination rates.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Among 6651 reported mpox cases, 561 (10.8%) were categorized as nonsexually acquired, with 12.5% hospitalized compared to 4.7% in the sexual exposure group. analysis.brief_en: A study presented at IDWeek 2026 analyzed mpox cases in California between May 2022 and December 2024, comparing those with nonsexual and sexual transmission. Researchers found that nonsexually acquired clade II mpox was associated with higher hospitalization rates (12.5% vs 4.7%), a higher prevalence of HIV (53.3% vs 39.8%), and lower vaccination rates compared to sexually acquired cases. Of 6651 reported cases, 561 (10.8%) were classified as nonsexually acquired, with notable demographic differences, including a higher proportion of individuals assigned female at birth and younger than 18 years. The study also highlighted socioeconomic disparities, with nonsexual cases more frequently occurring in areas with lower Health Performance Index (HPI) scores. The researchers concluded that more information is needed to understand the dynamics of non-sexual mpox transmission and develop targeted prevention strategies. All differences were considered statistically significant based on nonoverlapping 95% confidence intervals.

elements_zh.response_status_and_uncertainty: 该研究在IDWeek 2026上展示,所有报告的差异均基于不重叠的95%置信区间被认定为具有统计学意义。研究人员强调需要进一步研究非性传播猴痘 传播的动态,以制定针对性策略。

analysis_en.time: The study was conducted between May 2022 and December 2024, with the publication date on October 27, 2026.
analysis_en.location_and_population: The study focused on mpox cases in California, comparing patients with nonsexually acquired mpox to those with sexually acquired mpox, including demographic and clinical characteristics.
analysis_en.event: Researchers evaluated demographic and clinical differences between patients with sexually and nonsexually acquired clade II mpox in California, finding that nonsexually acquired cases were associated with higher hospitalization rates, higher HIV prevalence, and lower vaccination rates.
analysis_en.scale_impact_and_risk: Among 6651 reported mpox cases, 561 (10.8%) were categorized as nonsexually acquired, with 12.5% hospitalized compared to 4.7% in the sexual exposure group. HIV prevalence was 53.3% in the nonsexual group versus 39.8% in the sexual group. Vaccination rates were also lower in the nonsexual group (96.8% unvaccinated vs 87.9% in the sexual group).
analysis_en.response_status_and_uncertainty: The study was presented at IDWeek 2026, and all reported differences were considered statistically significant based on nonoverlapping 95% CIs. The researchers emphasized the need for further investigation into the dynamics of non-sexual mpox transmission for targeted strategies.

news.title_zh: 非性传播获得的猴痘与更高的住院率相关
news.source_body_en: A study presented at IDWeek 2026 analyzed mpox cases in California between May 2022 and December 2024, comparing those with nonsexual and sexual transmission. Researchers found that nonsexually acquired clade II mpox was associated with higher hospitalization rates (12.5% vs 4.7%), a higher prevalence of HIV (53.3% vs 39.8%), and lower vaccination rates compared to sexually acquired cases. Of 6651 reported cases, 561 (10.8%) were classified as nonsexually acquired, with notable demographic differences, including a higher proportion of individuals assigned female at birth and younger than 18 years. The study also highlighted socioeconomic disparities, with nonsexual cases more frequently occurring in areas with lower Health Performance Index (HPI) scores. The researchers concluded that more information is needed to understand the dynamics of non-sexual mpox transmission and develop targeted prevention strategies. All differences were considered statistically significant based on nonoverlapping 95% confidence intervals.
news.content_zh: 一项在IDWeek 2026上展示的研究分析了2022年5月至2024年12月期间加利福尼亚州的猴痘病例,比较了非性传播和性传播的传播病例。研究人员发现,非性传播获得的II型猴痘与更高的住院率(12.5% vs 4.7%)、更高的HIV 患病率(53.3% vs 39.8%)以及比性传播病例更低的疫苗接种率相关。在6651例报告病例中,有561例(10.8%)被归类为非性传播获得,具有显著的人口统计学差异,包括更多出生时被指定为女性的个体以及年龄小于18岁的个体。该研究还强调了社会经济差异,非性传播病例更常出现在健康表现指数(HPI)得分较低的地区。研究人员得出结论,需要更多信息来了解非性传播猴痘 传播的动态,并制定针对性的预防策略。所有差异均基于不重叠的95%置信区间被认定为具有统计学意义。

Borotho Image @WHO South Africa has recorded four additional mpox cases, bringing the total to 26 across five provinces. Symptoms include a rash, fever, headache, muscle aches, swollen lymph nodes and fatigue. The public is urged to avoid close contact with suspected cases, monitor symptoms after exposure and seek medical advice if concerned. The Department of Health has confirmed four additional cases of mpox in South Africa, bringing the total number of laboratory-confirmed cases in the country to 26. Of the 26 cases recorded, 18 were reported in the Western Cape, three in Gauteng, two in the Eastern Cape, two in the Free State and one in KwaZulu-Natal. Health Department spokesperson Foster Mohale said two of the 18 cases in the Western Cape involved foreign nationals who were visiting South Africa, while the remaining 16 were linked to local transmission. “Twenty-five of the 26 cases are male, aged between 23 to 50 years and a median age of 37 years. Clade and lineage information is currently available for 17 cases, of which 13 are associated with the Clade Ib mpox virus and four with Clade IIb,” Mohale said. Members of the public are urged to remain vigilant and seek medical attention if they develop symptoms associated with the illness. What are the symptoms of mpox? The Department of Health has advised the public to look out for the following symptoms: A rash, which may develop into blisters or sores. Fever. Headache. Muscle aches. Swollen lymph nodes. Fatigue. Anyone who suspects they have been in close contact with someone who has mpox is urged to seek medical advice and monitor themselves for symptoms for 21 days. “Should symptoms develop, they should avoid close contact with others and seek medical attention,” Mohale added. How can you protect yourself against mpox? Individuals should avoid close, skin-to-skin contact with anyone who has an mpox-like rash. People should also avoid sharing bedding, towels, clothing and other personal items with someone who has the infection. Healthcare workers are urged to maintain a high index of suspicion when assessing suspected cases and to follow infection prevention and control protocols. “The Department will continue to work closely with the National Institute for Communicable Diseases (NICD), provincial health authorities and other stakeholders to strengthen surveillance, case finding, contact tracing, risk communication and community engagement in order to contain further spread of mpox,” Mohale said. news.content: News Health Brazil to send additional mpox vaccine doses to Rio de Janeiro — The Rio Times Fedir Kryshtovskyi 01 November 2026 12:33 Brazil will send additional doses of the mpox vaccine to Rio de Janeiro following an increase in the number of registered cases. Health Minister Alexandre Padilha announced this on October 31, emphasizing that the country is not facing an outbreak at the national level. As The Rio Times reports , the city epidemiological center registered 45 mpox cases in September and another 29 in October 2026. A total of 74 cases were detected over the two months, compared with 10 during the same period in 2025. Preparation for mass events According to Padilha, the additional vaccines are intended to help control the current situation and prepare the city for major events at the end of the year. The minister noted that eligibility for vaccination will not be expanded and that no mass vaccination campaign will be conducted. Additional doses will be directed to areas where the number of cases is increasing. More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram . Since the beginning of 2026, Brazil has recorded 665 mpox cases. Padilha compared the current situation with 2022, when nearly 11,000 people were infected in the country, and stated that the current situation differs significantly from that outbreak. Who can receive the vaccine The mpox vaccine is not included in Brazil's national immunization schedule. It is recommended for laboratory workers who work with related viruses, people living with HIV and weakened immune systems, as well as people who have had direct medium- or high-risk contact with a probable or confirmed case of the disease, following a medical assessment. Mpox spreads primarily through direct contact with skin lesions, bodily fluids, or contaminated objects. Symptoms include fever, body aches, general malaise, and rashes that can develop into blisters. Read us on Download our app

news.source_body_en: Brazil has announced plans to send additional mpox vaccine doses to Rio de Janeiro following an increase in registered cases. The Health Minister, Alexandre Padilha, made the announcement on October 31, 2026, stating that the country is not facing a national outbreak. According to The Rio Times, the city's epidemiological center reported 45 mpox cases in September and 29 in October 2026, totaling 74 cases over the two months—compared to 10 cases during the same period in 2025. The mpox vaccine is not part of Brazil's national immunization schedule and is recommended for specific high-risk groups.
news.content_zh: 巴西宣布计划在注册病例增加后向里约热内卢运送额外的猴痘 疫苗剂量。卫生部长亚历山大·帕迪拉在2026年10月31日宣布了这一消息,表示该国并未面临全国性的暴发。据《里约时报》报道,里约热内卢的流行病学中心在2026年9月报告了45例猴痘病例,10月报告了29例,两个月共计74例——与2025年同期的10例相比。自2026年初以来,巴西已记录了665例猴痘病例。帕迪拉指出,当前的情况与2022年的暴发有显著不同,后者造成了近11,000例感染。这些额外的疫苗剂量旨在控制疫情传播,并为年底的重大活动做准备,但不会扩大疫苗接种的适用范围,也不会启动大规模的疫苗接种宣传活动。猴痘 疫苗不属于巴西的国家免疫接种计划,仅推荐用于特定的高风险群体。

supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Monday, November 2, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Chickenpox Virus Dominated Rash Illnesses Mistaken for Mpox in Sierra Leone by October 29, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 4 mins read 0 Chickenpox Virus Dominated Rash Illnesses Mistaken for Mpox in Sierra Leone Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram During Sierra Leone’s 2025 mpox epidemic, more than half of the patients who met the clinical case definition for mpox but tested negative for the mpox virus were carrying other rash-causing pathogens, with varicella-zoster virus — the agent of chickenpox and shingles — accounting for the vast majority of those detections. That is the central finding of a retrospective laboratory-based surveillance study published in New Microbes and New Infections, which screened samples from MPXV-negative suspected mpox cases using two commercial multiplex PCR panels across eight health districts. The study was conducted between June 16 and August 27, 2025, as part of the national epidemic response. Two mobile laboratories, deployed at the regional hospital in Port Loko and at the Koinadugu District Government Hospital, processed clinical specimens — predominantly lesion swabs, along with a small number of vaginal swabs and crust samples — from patients meeting the World Health Organization mpox case definition. During active case searching, the definition was broadened to include anyone presenting with a severe rash, even if other criteria were not met. In total, 407 suspected mpox cases were sampled and tested for MPXV by quantitative PCR during the study window. Of these, 144 were positive, corresponding to a positivity rate of 35.7 percent, and were excluded from the differential analysis. The remaining 263 MPXV-negative samples — 252 lesion swabs, seven vaginal swabs, and four crust samples — all passed an endogenous control quality check and were retained for further testing. The researchers used the Allplex Meningitis-V1 Assay, previously validated on cutaneous samples with next-generation sequencing, to detect seven herpesviruses: herpes simplex virus types 1 and 2, varicella-zoster virus, Epstein-Barr virus, cytomegalovirus, and human herpesviruses 6 and 7. A second panel, the Allplex Genital Ulcer Assay, targeted the bacteria Haemophilus ducreyi, Treponema pallidum, and Chlamydia trachomatis, the causative agent of lymphogranuloma venereum, alongside overlapping viral targets. A sample was considered positive if a target was detected with a cycle threshold value below 35, and weak or late amplification signals were re-tested in duplicate. For the four targets covered by both panels, duplicate testing yielded 100 percent concordance. The results showed that at least one target was identified in 153 of the 263 samples, an overall detection rate of 58.2 percent. Varicella-zoster virus was by far the most frequently detected pathogen, found in 43.3 percent of patients (114 of 263; 95 percent confidence interval 37.3 to 49.6). Among the other herpesviruses, HSV-2 showed the highest detection frequency at 7.2 percent, followed by cytomegalovirus at 6.85 percent and Epstein-Barr virus at 6.1 percent. Lower rates were recorded for HHV-7 (4.6 percent), HSV-1 (1.9 percent), and HHV-6 (0.4 percent). Among bacterial targets, Haemophilus ducreyi was detected in 1.1 percent of cases, while every sample tested negative for Treponema pallidum and Chlamydia trachomatis. The study population was young: ages ranged from 1 to 80 years with a median of 18 years, and 44.5 percent of participants were aged 15 or younger. Gender information was available for 259 participants, of whom 58.7 percent were male. Statistically significant associations with age emerged for Epstein-Barr virus and HSV-2, both detected at higher proportions in older age groups, with detection rising progressively across the three age strata. Cytomegalovirus and Epstein-Barr virus were the only pathogens showing significant sex-based differences, both more frequent among females. Varicella-zoster virus showed no significant demographic associations, although nearly 48 percent of children aged 15 or younger tested positive compared with 39 percent of patients over 30, a difference that did not reach statistical significance. Co-detections were common and often complex. Combinations involving varicella-zoster virus were the most frequent, occurring in 19 samples, most often alongside HSV-2 and cytomegalovirus. One sample was positive for five herpesviruses simultaneously — varicella-zoster virus, cytomegalovirus, HSV-2, HHV-7, and Epstein-Barr virus — and two samples carried triple viral infections. Haemophilus ducreyi was exclusively co-detected with varicella-zoster virus, on two occasions, a molecular co-detection the authors describe as rarely reported. Among co-detections not involving varicella-zoster virus, nine of ten included Epstein-Barr virus. The authors caution that, given the small numbers, no inference about biological interaction between co-detected pathogens can be made. Geographically, the highest sample numbers came from Port Loko and Tonkolili, and detections of at least one target exceeded undiagnosed cases in five of the eight surveyed districts. Varicella-zoster virus was the only pathogen identified in every district where positive cases were found, with the largest counts in Koinadugu, Falaba, and Port Loko. The distribution of other pathogens varied: HSV-2 and cytomegalovirus clustered in Port Loko and Tonkolili, Epstein-Barr virus in Kambia, and HHV-7 in Kambia and Bombali. One observation carries particular public health weight. The retrospective screening identified Haemophilus ducreyi in three samples collected months before an outbreak of Haemophilus ducreyi-associated skin ulceration was officially declared in Sierra Leone for the first time in December 2025, with the reported likely index case showing symptom onset on October 1, 2025. The authors stress that their findings do not establish an epidemiological link between these three patients and the subsequent outbreak, but they argue that real-time differential testing could potentially have provided an early warning signal prompting further investigation. The study has notable limitations. Samples and epidemiological data were originally collected for the mpox response, leaving critical clinical information — including symptoms, HIV status, and patient outcomes — incomplete, so the clinical impact of co-detections could not be assessed. MPXV-positive samples were not included in the differential testing, sequencing was not performed, and the study period covered neither the entire outbreak timeline nor every district in Sierra Leone. The authors also note that pathogen distributions can vary seasonally, meaning the findings represent a temporal snapshot rather than a complete annual profile, which may partly explain the absence of Chlamydia trachomatis and Treponema pallidum detections. Even so, the results demonstrate the feasibility of integrating multiplex molecular screening into outbreak response, particularly when combined with mobile laboratory deployment, to reduce diagnostic dead ends and uncover pathogens circulating beneath the epidemiological signal of a dominant outbreak agent. What happened Health Minister Alexandre Padilha said on Saturday 31 October 2026 that extra mpox vaccine is going to Rio de Janeiro. The numbers Rio city logged 74 cases in September and October 2026, against 10 in the same months of 2025. National picture Brazil has 665 cases in 2026; the minister rejects any comparison with 2022, when almost 11,000 were infected. Who can be vaccinated Only recommended groups, with no widening of eligibility and no mass campaign. Brazil is sending extra mpox vaccine to Rio de Janeiro after 74 cases in September and October 2026, against 10 a year earlier. Health Minister Alexandre Padilha announced the move on Saturday 31 October 2026 and said Brazil faces no national outbreak. For US readers, the news matters because Rio is a top travel destination and the ministry is preparing the city for large year-end gatherings. Our Rio de Janeiro city guide covers the city for travelers and residents. What Brazil Announced Padilha leads Brazil’s federal Ministry of Health, and on Saturday 31 October 2026 he announced a larger shipment of mpox vaccine to Rio de Janeiro. He said the aim is to control current cases and prepare the city for large year-end gatherings. The minister stressed that the vaccine stays aimed at the groups already recommended. There is no wider eligibility and no mass campaign, only extra doses where the curve is rising. How Fast Mpox Cases Are Rising in Rio The city’s epidemiology observatory counted 45 mpox cases in September and 29 in October 2026, a total of 74. In the same two months of 2025 the city counted only 10, so this year’s figure is more than seven times higher. Brazil as a whole has 665 cases so far in 2026, according to the minister. The rise in Rio is therefore a local flare-up inside a much smaller national total. Ipanema beach at sunset in Rio de Janeiro. (Photo: Rio Times library) Why the Minister Rejects the Word Outbreak In a social media post that day, Padilha compared the 2026 situation with 2022, when Brazil’s mpox outbreak reached almost 11,000 infected people. He called the current picture very different from that outbreak. He added that the ministry keeps active surveillance together with states and cities. In his words, the public health system, known as the SUS, is ready to diagnose, treat and monitor cases. Who Can Get the Mpox Vaccine The mpox vaccine is not part of Brazil’s routine immunization calendar, the National Immunization Program. The Ministry of Health says the mpox vaccine is meant for groups at higher risk of severe illness, depending on supply. Those groups are laboratory workers who handle related viruses and people with HIV, the virus that weakens the immune system, whose immunity is already weak. People with direct medium- or high-risk contact with a suspected or confirmed case can also be vaccinated after a health assessment. What Mpox Is and How It Spreads Mpox is a viral disease that starts with fever, body aches and a general feeling of illness. Skin lesions follow and can turn into blisters. The virus spreads mainly through direct contact with lesions, body fluids and contaminated objects. The Ministry of Health says most cases are mild to moderate, most people improve within two to four weeks, and no specific drug is approved. What It Means for You The ministry says mpox spreads mainly through close contact, and the minister puts Brazil’s national count at 665 cases in 2026. Anyone with skin lesions plus fever or swollen glands, or with close contact with a case, should go to a health unit. Under the ministry’s rules, the vaccine goes only to the risk groups above, so ordinary tourists are not on the list. Travelers living with HIV who plan to visit Rio can ask their own doctor about the vaccine before the trip. What Is Not Known The ministry has not said how many extra doses are going to Rio or when they will arrive. It is also unknown whether the rise will continue into November and December. The ministry’s statement does not explain the jump in Rio. No decision to widen who can be vaccinated has been announced. More: Brazil news in English, every day from The Rio Times. Frequently Asked Questions Is there an mpox outbreak in Brazil? The health minister says it does not. Brazil has 665 cases in 2026, against almost 11,000 infections in the 2022 outbreak. How many mpox cases does Rio de Janeiro have? The city logged 74 cases in September and October 2026, against 10 in the same months of 2025. September had 45 and October 29. Who can get the mpox vaccine in Brazil? Laboratory workers who handle related viruses, people with HIV and weak immunity, and people with direct medium- or high-risk contact with a case. The mpox vaccine is not in the routine calendar. Should tourists avoid Rio de Janeiro? Mpox spreads mainly through close contact with lesions, body fluids or contaminated objects. Anyone with symptoms after exposure should go to a health unit. What are the symptoms of mpox? Skin lesions, fever, body aches, headache and swollen glands are the main signs, and lesions can become blisters. Most people improve in two to four weeks. supplementary_news.content: TODAY’S PAPER | November 02, 2026 | EPAPER ☰ Home Latest Pakistan Business World Sports Opinion Life & Style T-Magazine Blogs Tech Cartoon Home Sindh Mpox caseload in Sindh soars past 100 Woman shifted to ICU at Nipa hospital; govt reviews surveillance measures Our Correspondent October 29, 2026 1 min read facebook twitter whatsup linkded email K-P reported first locally transmitted MPOX case. PHOTO: FILE KARACHI: Sindh has reported another case of mpox, prompting the Health Department to convene a meeting to review surveillance, early diagnosis and measures to contain the spread of the virus. A woman who tested positive for mpox has been shifted to the intensive care unit (ICU) of the Sindh Infectious Diseases Hospital at Nipa. According to hospital officials, she was brought to the facility two days ago, where samples were collected for a polymerase chain reaction (PCR) test. The infection was confirmed after the test results became available. Hospital officials said seven mpox patients were currently receiving treatment at the facility. According to figures available with the Health Department, Sindh has reported 98 mpox cases and 12 deaths so far this year. However, sources said the latest case had taken the cumulative number of infections reported during the year beyond 100. Against this backdrop, a meeting of Health Department officials was convened under the chairmanship of the director general Health Services Sindh to review the situation and assess measures to prevent further transmission. Attendees at the meeting included the director Health Services Karachi Division, a professor of pathology at Dow University and director of the Provincial Public Health Laboratory Sindh, Professor Dr Saeed Khan. The chief executive officer of the Sindh Healthcare Commission was also invited, while Additional Director of the Provincial Disease Surveillance and Response Unit (PDSRU) Sindh, Dr Asif Syed. Participants reviewed arrangements for monitoring cases, identifying suspected patients at an early stage and ensuring timely reporting of infections. Discussions also focused on laboratory testing of suspected cases, identifying people who had come into contact with infected individuals and ensuring their continued monitoring. Officials further examined measures to strengthen infection prevention and control at public and private hospitals and healthcare centres, improve early diagnosis and ensure that confirmed and suspected cases were promptly reported to the relevant authorities. supplementary_news.content: Dangerous Mpox Strain Found Abroad May Be Spreading in Central California A more dangerous strain of mpox may be spreading within California's Stanislaus County. Health officials announced four reported cases, with two confirmed as clade I and two awaiting results. Three of the four people had not traveled outside the country. Clade I is typically associated with international travel and can cause more serious illness than clade II, especially among immunocompromised people. Its mortality rate ranges between 1 percent and 10 percent. Officials say the risk to the general public remains low. Mpox usually spreads through close skin-to-skin contact. It can cause fever, muscle weakness and painful sores resembling pimples or blisters. Symptoms can begin 21 days after exposure and last between two and four weeks. People diagnosed should isolate until their rash disappears. Health officials recommend recognizing symptoms, getting vaccinated if at risk of exposure and seeking medical care when needed. Most people recover on their own, but severe cases can be treated with antivirals. Vaccination appointments are available through the Stanislaus County Immunization Clinic

REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration/File Photo comments Join our Whatsapp Channel KARACHI: Another child tested positive for mpox in the city on Friday, raising the tally of the viral infectious disease this year so far in the province to 115. Mpox is a viral infection which was earlier restricted to international travellers. It spreads through close contact with someone who has mpox, contaminated bedding, towels, medical instruments, surfaces or objects. Sources said the three-year-old boy was currently under treatment at Sindh Infectious Diseases Hospital and Research Centre (SIDH&RC). “Like the recent two cases, this child also underwent circumcision at the same Malir hospital that has been officially sealed over concerns related to lack of infection control measures,” a hospital doctor said, adding that an infant with mpox died early this week after remaining under treatment for 10 days at the facility while another was in the intensive care. He also shared that the seven mpox patients currently under treatment at SIDH&RC included the mother and an aunt of the infant who died fighting mpox — the first infant’s death in Karachi this year. With the latest case, the total number of mpox cases reported this year so far at SIDH&RC has risen to 31, while in the province to 115 with 12 deaths. The Sindh Health Care Commission (SHCC) had sealed Ibne Hassan Hospital over 10 days ago following a laboratory report confirming an mpox case in an infant, after concerns were identified regarding infection prevention and control practices. “The hospital was legal but not registered with the SHCC. The team sealed the facility following reports that a child seemed to have contracted mpox there. The team during inspection found a dispenser conducting circumcision, a procedure that was beyond his scope,” explained Dr Ahson Qavi Siddiqi, the chief executive officer of SHCC. The hospital, he said, was opened on Friday for sanitisation, fumigation and disinfection, and sealed again. “This exercise will continue for some time and then sampling [to see if the facility is safe and fit for operation] will be carried out. The concerned party is also required to submit certain legal documents, too. All this will lead to a decision on the case.” Published in Dawn, October 31st, 2026 Most Popular 01 Pakistani three-wheelers go international as automotive manufacturer opens plant in Philippines 02 Capt Safdar's remarks about women suffering from illness draw criticism, including from CM Maryam 03 US hears Pakistan’s concerns over terrorism from Afghanistan, would play ‘productive role’ if there is one: Rubio 04 CDA directs removal of 'unauthorised' construction at JUI-F chief's residence in Islamabad 05 Netanyahu's bloc finishes ahead in Israel election, but well short of majority 06 CDF Munir, Singapore's FM discuss regional security and bilateral cooperation 07 ‘Very little, if anything, done for KP’: PM Shehbaz rails against PTI’s governance in province 08 DG ISPR says Pakistan 'cautiously optimistic' on US-Iran mediation 09 China green channel Latest Stories Lazio pull clear at Serie A summit as Gattuso warns of vertigo Antonelli becomes youngest F1 champion at 20 years old Mbappe strikes after China controversy as Real Madrid beat Santander in La Liga Lyon, Paris FC close in on PSG at top of Ligue 1 Arsenal claim Premier League top spot as Havertz seals win at Liverpool Crew from Nasa's simulated Mars mission emerges after 378 days in isolation Opinion Uncertain local governments Ahmed Bilal Mehboob The ECP is battling both the federal and provincial governments that are reluctant to hold LG polls. supplementary_news.content: TODAY’S PAPER | November 02, 2026 | EPAPER ☰ Home Latest Pakistan Business World Sports Opinion Life & Style T-Magazine Blogs Tech Cartoon Home Khyber Pakhtunkhwa K-P reports four new mpox cases Health authorities step up contact tracing as tally tops 18 Shahida Parveen October 28, 2026 1 min read facebook twitter whatsup linkded email K-P reported first locally transmitted MPOX case. PHOTO: FILE PESHAWAR: Four new mpox cases have been reported in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, taking the provincial tally for the year to 18 and prompting health authorities to trace the patients' contacts amid concerns about ocal transmission. None of the patients, including one woman and three men, has a reported history of international travel, the health department said. Samples sent to the Public Health Reference Laboratory at Khyber Medical University confirmed the infections. Two patients are from Nowshera, one from Peshawar and one from Mardan. All four have been advised to isolate at home to prevent further spread. One patient has died and 13 have recovered from mpox in the province this year, according to the health department. The first case was reported on January 9. People with mpox are infectious and can pass the disease on to others until all sores have healed and a new layer of skin has formed. Children, pregnant people and people with weak immune systems are at risk for complications from mpox. Typically for mpox, fever, muscle aches and sore throat appear first. The mpox rash begins on the face and spreads over the body, extending to the palms of the hands and soles of the feet and evolves over 2-4 weeks in stages – macules, papules, vesicles, pustules. Lesions dip in the centre before crusting over. Scabs then fall off. Lymphadenopathy (swollen lymph nodes) is a classic feature of mpox. Some people can be infected without developing any symptoms. In the context of the global outbreak of mpox which began in 2022 (caused mostly by Clade IIb virus), the illness begins differently in some people. In just over a half of cases, a rash may appear before or at the same time as other symptoms and does not always progress over the body. The first lesion can be in the groin, anus, or in or around the mouth. People with mpox can become very sick. Onstage in Pasadena This Week Virtual Guide to Pasadena Area Schools Guide to Summer Camps Community News Pasadena City Manager Proclaims Monkeypox a Local Emergency Published on Thursday, August 18, 2022 | 4:35 pm Monkeypox Virus courtesy of PPHD Interim City Manager Cynthia Kurtz has proclaimed a local emergency to strengthen the City’s preparedness and ability to respond to the virus. In an effort to stop the spread of monkeypox and make the monkeypox vaccine more readily accessible to those at highest risk, Pasadena Public Health Department (PPHD) is also expanding the eligibility criteria for the vaccine, effective immediately. “We are continuing to work proactively to protect the health of our community, and this proclamation allows us to mobilize more resources,” Kurtz said. “This local emergency will allow us to continue to support our community members who are currently most at-risk, while also to better prepare for what’s to come.” Currently, PPHD has 15 confirmed or probable cases of monkeypox in Pasadena. There are reportedly 2,356 cases in California as of Aug. 17, according to the California Department of Public Health. The proclamation allows the City to take all actions necessary to implement preventive measures to protect and preserve public health, including, but not limited to, mobilizing City resources, accelerating emergency planning; streamlining staffing; coordinating across other agencies; expediting the ability of the City to purchase necessary supplies to combat monkeypox; allowing for future reimbursement by the state and federal governments; and raising awareness throughout Pasadena about monkeypox, including how people can lower their risk and stop the spread. Earlier this month, Governor Gavin Newsom proclaimed a state of emergency to support the state’s response to monkeypox. Additionally, Los Angeles and Orange Counties have issued similar proclamations to bolster their preparedness. PPHD continues to provide monkeypox vaccines by invitation only to the following select groups of persons identified through public health investigation: • Gay or bisexual men and transgender persons who had multiple or anonymous sex partners in the last 14 days, including engaging in survival and/or transactional sex (e.g., sex in exchange for shelter, food and other goods and needs).Persons confirmed to have had high- or intermediate-risk contact with someone with monkeypox, as defined by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). • Persons who attended an event/venue where there was high risk of exposure to an individual(s) with confirmed monkeypox virus through skin-to-skin or sexual contact. Public health officials will work with event/venue organizers to identify persons who may have been present and at risk of exposure while at the venue. • Persons experiencing homelessness (PEH) with high-risk behaviors. • People in high-risk cohorts identified by clinical staff in the LA County Jail system. • Gay or bisexual men and transgender persons who: – Were diagnosed with gonorrhea or early syphilis within the past 12 months; or – Are on HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP); or – Attended or worked at a commercial sex venue or other venue where they had anonymous sex or sex with multiple partners (e.g., saunas, bathhouses, sex clubs, sex parties) within past 21 days. Vaccine eligibility and information on how to access vaccines will continue to be updated at www.cityofpasadena.net/monkeypox. Monkeypox is a viral infection that can spread through contact with body fluids, monkeypox sores, or shared items (such as clothing and bedding) that have been contaminated with fluids from sores of a person with monkeypox. Although monkeypox is not generally considered a sexually transmitted infection, it can be transmitted during sex through prolonged skin-to-skin and other intimate contact, regardless of gender or sexual orientation. To prevent the spread of monkeypox, PPHD recommends: • Avoiding close physical contact with people who have symptoms, including sores or rashes; • Talking to your sexual partner(s) about any recent illness and being aware of new or unexplained sores or rashes; • Avoiding contact with contaminated materials; • Wearing personal protective equipment (i.e., mask, gloves, gown) if you cannot avoid close contact with someone who has symptoms; • Practicing good hand hygiene; • Speaking to your healthcare provider about getting tested if you have symptoms; and • Staying in isolation until you are no longer considered infectious per public health guidance. For questions regarding monkeypox, public health officials recommend that you speak to your primary care provider. If you do not have a regular provider, call LA County 211 for assistance. In addition, people without a regular provider that have developed a rash in the genital or perianal area, can access services at Los Angeles County’s sexual health clinics. For more information on monkeypox, please visit www.cityofpasadena.net/monkeypox. Get our daily Pasadena newspaper in your email box. Free. At least 2 cases of mpox confirmed in Stanislaus County, health officials say KCRA / KQCA US LIVE Current Time 0:00 / Total Duration 0:36 Sorry, this video is not available, please check back later. Advertisement Updated: 5:07 PM PDT Oct 29, 2026 Editorial Standards i Nijzel Dotson Digital Producer At least 2 cases of mpox confirmed in Stanislaus County, health officials say Updated: 5:07 PM PDT Oct 29, 2026 Editorial Standards i Nijzel Dotson Digital Producer At least two cases of mpox, formerly known as monkeypox, have been confirmed in Stanislaus County, according to health officials. The Stanislaus County Health Services Agency said four cases of Clade 1 mpox were recently reported to them, with two of them confirmed by the California Department of Public Health. Advertisement There is additionally testing underway to possibly confirm the other two cases, health officials said. Stanislaus County HSA said three of the people tested reported no recent international travel and the travel history of the fourth person is still being investigated. Clade 1 mpox cases in the U.S. were commonly linked to international travel, but Stanislaus County HSA said since August, more cases have been reported among people without recent trips outside of the country. Still, health officials said the risk to the public remains low and there is no evidence that suggests mpox is spreading across California or the U.S. "While we have identified four cases in our county, we want residents to know that the risk to the general public remains low," said Stanislaus County Public Health Officer Dr. Thea Pasasozomentos. "Being aware of the symptoms, getting vaccinated if at risk of exposure to mpox, and seeking medical care when needed are important ways to protect yourself and prevent the spread of mpox. Mpox can be spread through close contact like touching or sex or contaminated materials like sheets, clothing and needles. Initial symptoms include fever, chills, exhaustion, and muscle weakness, followed by a painful or itchy rash with raised lesions that scab over. supplementary_news.content: News Health Three-year-old boy diagnosed with mpox in Karachi — Dawn UA.NEWS 31 October 2026 09:02 A three-year-old boy in Karachi, Pakistan, has been confirmed to have mpox. This brought the number of infection cases registered in Sindh province since the beginning of the year to 115, Dawn reports . Treatment of the child According to the publication's sources, the boy is being treated at the Sindh Infectious Diseases Hospital and Research Centre. A doctor at the facility said that the child, like two recent patients, underwent circumcision at a hospital in Malir district, which was sealed over concerns about compliance with infection-control measures. According to the doctor, an infant with mpox died at the centre early this week after 10 days of treatment. Another patient was in the intensive care unit. Among the seven patients currently being treated at the centre are the mother and aunt of the deceased infant. Hospital inspection Including the new patient, the centre in Karachi has recorded 31 mpox cases since the beginning of the year. Sindh province has registered 115 infection cases and 12 deaths. More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram . More than 10 days ago, the Sindh Healthcare Commission sealed Ibn Hassan Hospital after laboratory confirmation of mpox in an infant and due to identified shortcomings in infection prevention and control measures. The commission's chief executive officer, Ahsan Qavi Siddiqui, said that the medical facility was operating legally but was not registered with the commission. During the inspection, he said, officials found an employee performing circumcisions beyond the scope of their authority. The hospital was temporarily reopened for sanitisation, fumigation and disinfection, and was then sealed again. Once this work is completed, samples are planned to be taken there to determine whether the facility is safe and fit to operate. Read us on Download our app

supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Monday, November 2, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Only 6% of Primary Care Physicians in North-Western Nigeria Show Good Knowledge of Mpox, Survey Finds by October 27, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 3 mins read 0 Only 6% of Primary Care Physicians in North-Western Nigeria Show Good Knowledge of Mpox, Survey Finds Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Only 5.8% of primary care physicians surveyed in North-Western Nigeria demonstrated good knowledge of Mpox, according to an online cross-sectional study published in BMC Health Services Research. The finding, drawn from 155 doctors working in family medicine and pediatric outpatient settings across all seven states of the zone, points to a substantial gap in the preparedness of the clinicians most likely to encounter the first suspicious cases of a re-emerging zoonotic disease. The study set out to quantify how well this frontline workforce in northwestern Nigeria understands the disease, and to identify which sociodemographic and professional characteristics are associated with better knowledge. The participants were an experienced group. Their mean age was 38.8 years with a standard deviation of 7.4, and 60.7% were men. Most respondents, 77.4%, worked in general outpatient clinics, 63.2% had accumulated at least ten years of practice experience, and 36.1% were senior registrars. Despite this seniority profile, only 18.9% reported any prior experience diagnosing or managing a Mpox case, a detail that helps contextualize the knowledge results that followed. When knowledge was scored, the results were strikingly low. Just nine of the 155 participants, or 5.8%, achieved the threshold the investigators defined as good knowledge of Mpox. Discover more Track Outbreaks Book Care Services Check Symptoms Read Med Journals The mean overall knowledge score across the cohort was 61.7%, with a standard deviation of 12.5 percentage points, indicating that the typical physician answered roughly three-fifths of the knowledge items correctly. The authors conclude that this represents a significant gap in participants’ understanding of the various aspects of the disease. The inferential analysis identified three factors associated with higher mean knowledge scores. Physicians with ten or more years of practice experience scored significantly higher than their less experienced colleagues, with a p-value of 0.049. Senior professional cadres also performed better, an association that reached statistical significance at p = 0.031. Most notably, doctors who had been involved in diagnosing or managing Mpox at some point in their careers showed higher knowledge scores, with p = 0.021. Even so, the authors emphasize that these higher scores remained suboptimal, meaning that experience and seniority improved knowledge only partially and did not bring most clinicians to a good-knowledge standard. The cross-sectional design imposes important limits on how these findings can be interpreted. Because data were collected at a single point in time through an online survey, the study can describe associations but cannot establish causal relationships between professional characteristics and knowledge. The sample, while adequate for the calculated minimum of 153 participants at a 5% margin of error and 95% confidence level, was drawn from one geopolitical zone of Nigeria, and the authors note that the scarcity of comparable studies in northwestern Nigeria makes it difficult to benchmark these results against regional or national patterns. The finding that only about one in five participants had ever been directly involved in Mpox diagnosis or management suggests that many physicians in the region have had little practical exposure to reinforce whatever theoretical training they received. Discover more Buy Maps Shop African Art Get Health Tips health Health The survey employed a multi-stage sampling technique to reach physicians in Family Medicine/General Outpatient and Pediatric Outpatient Clinics across hospitals in the seven states, with the initial sample size target raised from 153 to 170 to allow for a 10% non-response buffer; 155 physicians ultimately completed the pretested online questionnaire, a completion rate of 91.2%. Data were analyzed descriptively and inferentially using Epi Info version 7. The authors call for targeted educational interventions to enhance the preparedness of primary care physicians to identify and coordinate Mpox cases in primary care settings. As primary care physicians serve as gatekeepers in the healthcare system, the study’s central message is a measured but sobering one: the frontline clinicians expected to serve as the system’s early warning for this zoonotic disease, at least in North-Western Nigeria, currently demonstrate limited knowledge of it, and closing that gap will require deliberate training rather than assumptions that experience alone will suffice. supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Monday, November 2, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Most Burundians know mpox, but many still mistake its cause, survey finds by October 27, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 3 mins read 0 Most Burundians know mpox, but many still mistake its cause, survey finds Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A nationwide cross-sectional survey in Burundi has found that while nearly all respondents had heard of mpox, substantial gaps persist in understanding what causes the disease, and most people did not know a vaccine exists. The nationwide cross-sectional survey interviewed 5,177 participants aged 15 years and older across five provinces of Burundi between March and December 2025. The survey used a structured questionnaire adapted from the Africa CDC behavioural and social sciences framework for mpox. Overall, 94.7 percent of participants had heard about mpox. Recognition of symptoms was strong: 94.4 percent correctly identified skin rash and 84.3 percent identified fever as common symptoms, and 86.6 percent recognized direct contact as a mode of transmission. Knowledge of the causative agent was markedly weaker. Some 21.4 percent of participants incorrectly identified bacteria as the cause of mpox, which is caused by a virus, and 24.5 percent did not know the causative agent at all. Taken together, nearly half of those surveyed held an incorrect view or no view on what causes the disease. Discover more Check Symptoms Read Med Journals Buy Maps Shop African Art Radio emerged as the dominant channel for health information, cited as the main source of mpox information by 82.0 percent of participants and as the most trusted source by 87.0 percent. The researchers analysed factors associated with knowledge and with prevention and control practices using bivariate and multivariable analyses, applying modified Poisson regression models with generalized estimating equations. Higher income was associated with better mpox knowledge, while prevention and control practices varied by knowledge level, income, marital status, and HIV status. Vaccine awareness was low despite apparent readiness to accept immunization. Although 86.1 percent of participants were unaware that an mpox vaccine is available, 76.5 percent reported willingness to accept vaccination if it were offered to them. The survey’s context matters. Mpox remains an important public health concern in Africa, particularly following the spread of clade Ib in several countries, and limited information had previously been available on Burundian population knowledge, risk perception, preventive behaviours, and willingness to accept mpox vaccination. The study was designed to assess social and behavioural factors associated with mpox preparedness among the general population. The authors caution that sampling weights were not applied, so the findings should be interpreted as estimates among surveyed participants rather than nationally weighted population estimates. Univariate analyses were used to describe key variables, and the cross-sectional design captures a snapshot rather than changes over time. The overall picture is one of high awareness paired with incomplete understanding. Most people surveyed knew the disease, its main symptoms, and its principal route of transmission, yet misconceptions about the causative agent were widespread, and knowledge was unevenly distributed across income groups. Discover more Explore History Find Vaccines vaccine The researchers conclude that, despite high awareness and willingness to accept vaccination, important gaps in mpox knowledge remain, particularly among lower-income groups, and that strengthening accessible and targeted risk communication strategies will be essential to improve mpox preparedness in Burundi.
